mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate environment compresses discount rates for equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the central bank maintains accommodative policy.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.1%.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated unemployment rates above 8.0% signal weak labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 8.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts and consumer spending (measured by RSAFS) indicate a weakening demand environment that triggers a negative equity market reaction over the next 60 days as recession risks rise.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative 60-day returns with a Rank IC below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, declining industrial production signals weakening manufacturing activity that precedes corporate profit deterioration, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of late-cycle expansion periods despite declining INDPRO.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 0.25% signals the start of monetary tightening, which increases borrowing costs and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of real personal consumption (RSAFS) reflects strong consumer demand that supports corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when RSAFS exceeds its 2009-2010 average.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in employment growth (PAYEMS) and rising unemployment (UNRATE) signal a deteriorating labor market that reduces consumer confidence and spending, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in PAYEMS and rise in UNRATE fails to predict negative 20-day returns with a Rank IC below 0.04 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a post-shock recovery regime, a low federal funds rate (below 0.25%) supports asset price appreciation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as the economy recovers from the financial crisis.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods during the post-shock recovery regime with FEDFUNDS below 0.25%.
